subject: zoology_2
question_text: Which hormone is called anti-diuretic hormone? Write the name of the gland that secretes it.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.52, VSAQ 90. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05 (examiner audit Z2-08): the insider note now asks for the posterior lobe of the pituitary by name instead of ruling the pituitary out, since the neurohypophysis is a lobe of that gland, and the s2 margin note now matches the single name the step prints.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The hormone
steps.why: Diuresis means passing a lot of urine, so a hormone that stops it is called anti-diuretic.
common_mistakes: Naming oxytocin. That is the other posterior pituitary hormone.
steps.memory_tip: Vasopressin holds water back, so it is anti-diuretic.
steps.margin_note: One line each. Both are marked.

steps.label: The gland
steps.why: It is made in the hypothalamus but stored and released by the posterior lobe, which is the part that secretes it.
common_mistakes: Naming the anterior pituitary. It is the posterior lobe.
Naming the kidney, which is where it acts, not where it is made.
steps.memory_tip: Neurohypophysis is the back part of the pituitary.
steps.margin_note: Name the posterior lobe: the neurohypophysis.

lines.text: It is secreted by the neurohypophysis

insider_note: One mark for the hormone, one for the gland. Both must appear. Name the posterior lobe of the pituitary — the neurohypophysis — rather than the pituitary alone, so the marker sees which lobe you mean.
